beats.anchor: Le monsieur colle deux rustines, des petits pansements de caoutchouc, en sifflotant.
beats.extras: The tyre repairman of the crossroads (about 50): a wiry man with very dark skin, short grey hair, oil-stained blue work overalls with rolled sleeves, a rag over one shoulder, whistling with puckered lips.
beats.outfit: BriBri in his sun-yellow T-shirt with one vertical red stripe on the left side of the chest, green shorts with a thin white side stripe, his red sock on his RIGHT foot and his yellow sock on his LEFT foot, scuffed white trainers, small soft round afro. Papa Armand (41), tall, short neat beard, in a light blue short-sleeved shirt and olive trousers.
beats.action: Sitting on an upturned crate, the repairman presses a small round rubber patch onto the deflated rubber bladder of the ball laid across his knee, whistling. BriBri, on tiptoe right next to him, leans in so close his nose almost touches it, eyes huge with hope, hands clasped. Papa stands just behind with his hands in his pockets, smiling at his son.
beats.location: A roadside tyre repair stand at a crossroads in Bafoussam: stacks of old motorbike tyres, a hand pump, a basin of water, a wooden bench; green hills and red earth roads behind, a motorbike taxi parked.
beats.light: Cool highland morning, the last white mist lifting from the hills, soft golden sun on the faces.
beats.camera: Medium shot at BriBri's eye level, the patch and the bladder sharp in the centre between the repairman's fingers and BriBri's face.
beats.alt: Au carrefour, le réparateur de pneus colle deux rustines sur la vessie du ballon, sous les yeux immenses de BriBri.

beats.anchor: Il s'arrête, le ballon de sachets sous le pied.
beats.extras: A brown-and-white goat half swallowed by the fog, looking offended. Far away, two or three faint grey silhouettes of village boys calling with cupped hands, impossible to recognise.
beats.outfit: BriBri in his sun-yellow T-shirt with the red stripe, green shorts, his red sock on his RIGHT foot and his yellow sock on his LEFT foot, scuffed white trainers, small soft round afro beaded with tiny drops of mist. Under his foot, a homemade ball of plastic bags rolled up and tied with rubber bands (not Mami's ball).
beats.action: BriBri has stopped dead in the middle of a white void, one foot on the plastic-bag ball, his whole body frozen, head turned to one side to listen, eyes wide, mouth slightly open: he is completely lost. Around him only a few stalks of maize and the head of the goat emerge from the fog.
beats.location: A steep slope of short grass between two maize fields near Bafoussam, a goal made of two sticks barely visible at the top of the slope.
beats.light: Late afternoon, thick milky fog diffusing a soft white light, no shadows, the yellow of BriBri's T-shirt the only strong colour in the frame.
beats.camera: Wide quiet shot, BriBri small in the lower centre of a huge white space, the goat on the left, the faint silhouettes in the far upper right.
beats.alt: Perdu dans le brouillard, BriBri s'arrête, le pied sur le ballon de sachets, et écoute les voix qui l'appellent.

beats.anchor: Elle la tend, à deux mains, à une jeune femme du premier rang, un bébé endormi dans son dos.
beats.extras: Maman Tchinda (about 25): a young woman with dark brown skin and a short natural haircut under a small headwrap, in a blue-and-white wax-print dress, a baby asleep on her back in a tied cloth, laughing and crying at once. Mama Kemadjou, the treasurer (about 55): a very tall, very thin woman with glasses, in the same blue-and-white wax print, holding a thick black notebook against her chest. Behind them, rows of women of all ages in matching blue-and-white wax-print dresses and headwraps, seated on plastic chairs and benches, clapping.
beats.outfit: Mami Nyanga (68), small and very straight, in her red-and-yellow wax-print dress and matching headscarf, sandals. BriBri in his sun-yellow T-shirt with the red stripe and green shorts, his red sock on his RIGHT foot and yellow sock on his LEFT foot. Kaydoudou in a plain forest-green T-shirt, thin shaved part on the left side of his head, a pencil behind his ear.
beats.action: Standing behind a small wooden table, Mami lifts a metal cash box painted green with both hands and holds it out to Maman Tchinda, who reaches for it, overwhelmed. The women around clap and sing. On a bench at the side, BriBri watches open-mouthed, and Kaydoudou leans forward, elbows on his knees, thinking hard.
beats.location: Mami's courtyard in Bafoussam: swept beaten earth, a hibiscus hedge, a mango tree, plastic chairs and benches, dishes covered with cloths on a table.
beats.light: Sunday late morning, warm sun filtering through the mango leaves, dappled light on the blue-and-white dresses, the green box catching a bright reflection.
beats.camera: Medium shot at seated eye level, the green box at the centre between Mami's hands and Maman Tchinda's, the brothers on the right edge.
beats.alt: Mami tend la caisse verte du njangi à Maman Tchinda, qui rit et pleure à la fois, sous les yeux des deux frères.
